title: runtime-version-gating-and-safe-rollback-strategy
content:
Purpose
This is a practical playbook for performing controlled runtime and control-plane upgrades for Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. Focus is on gating, automated verification, and deterministic rollback so customers experience minimal disruption. This doc is intentionally operational — checklists, commands, and measurable verification gates.

Scope
- Runtime binary / inference engine upgrades (x.y -> x.y+1)
- Control plane API and agent changes that affect on-prem components
- Terraform module changes that touch networking, instance templates, or stateful volumes
- NOT in-scope: model weights/bundle promotions (handled by model rollout playbooks)

Executive summary (one-paragraph)
Upgrade principle: never rely on a single binary flip. Gate by version-aware routing, small-scale canary, observable SLO checks, and a reversible migration path. When stateful schema changes are required, decouple schema migration from runtime cutover (two-phase commit: prepare-migrate-verify, then cutover). If any validation gate fails, traffic should automatically divert to the previous known-good variant and the upgrade should be aborted.

Quick checklist (preflight, 24-48h prior)
1) Open incident channel: #private-upgrades and create an incident room (post the upgrade RFC link).
2) Confirm customer maintenance windows and pre-approval for failover (if required).
3) Backup control-plane databases and object stores: export meta and put incremental snapshot in immutable storage. Record snapshot ID.
4) Verify Terraform plan: run terraform plan with the "upgrade-audit" var set. Save plan output.
5) Run smoke tests against a mirrored staging cluster using the exact upgrade artifacts and terraform plan.
6) Confirm monitoring alert thresholds and synthetic tests are enabled (latency p50/p95, error-rate, token-throttle).
7) Verify KMS/HSM access for the new control-plane agent; rotate test keys in staging first.
8) Document rollback criteria and assign an owner for rollback execution.

Gating matrix (pass/fail checks for canary promotion)
- Health: agent heartbeat and API liveness ok for 10m
- Latency: p95 token latency <= baseline * 1.25 over 30m
- Errors: 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.5% absolute
- Cost/Throughput: sustained throughput within expected range; batching efficiency not worse than -10%
- Functional: prompt set regression score >= baseline - 1% (automated eval harness)
- KV cache compatibility: no missing keys for synthetic scenarios

Canary rollout sequence (recommended)
Step 0: Prepare artifacts and manifest (build tag, docker images, runtime checksum, terraform module sha).
Step 1: Create versioned control-plane agent image and store in private registry with immutable tag.
Step 2: Apply Terraform in a non-destructive mode to create a parallel canary pool (new instance group or node pool) with 5-10% of capacity. Use module flag: upgrade_mode = "gated-canary".
Step 3: Register canary instances with smart router via API: set routing policy weight to 5-10% for new version, 90-95% to baseline.
Step 4: Run live-synthetic traffic: replay 1h of recorded request traces at low concurrency then ramp to normal canary load.
Step 5: Run full validation suite (functional, perf, security e2e) against canary for 45-60 minutes.
Step 6: If gates pass for 60 minutes, increment weight to 25% and re-evaluate for 30 minutes. On success, proceed to 100% in staged increments (25 -> 50 -> 100).
Step 7: When at 100%, keep the old baseline instances on standby for at least 2 hours before decommission.

Automated rollback triggers (immediate)
- Any 5xx spike exceeding gating threshold
- Latency p95 breach for 3 consecutive evaluation windows
- Failed functional regression tests during canary
- Missing or malformed KV cache reads for >0.1% of traffic
When triggered: set routing weights back to baseline 100% (API call), scale canary pool to zero, and run root-cause capture (logs/jarvis trace snapshot).

Terraform module notes (practical tips)
- Use soft flags: add new resources rather than mutating existing ones when possible (create new instance group + attach then detach old group).
- Recommended variables: upgrade_mode (gated-canary | blue-green | immediate), preserve_instance_templates = true, bootstrap_timeout = "20m".
- Example snippet for creating a canary pool:

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "runtime_canary" {
  name = var.cluster_name + "-runtime-canary"
  desired_capacity = ceil(var.desired_capacity * 0.08)
  launch_template = aws_launch_template.runtime_canary.id
  lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }
}

- State handling: do not rotate stateful EBS volumes in the same apply; prefer attach-new-volume pattern and replicate data using rsync/volume-snapshots.
- Drift checks: run terraform show | grep -A3 "lifecycle" in CI and post the diff to the preflight channel.

Database and stateful migrations
- If schema change required: run a read-only compatibility migration first (backwards-compatible migration), keep old runtime able to read both formats.
- Two-phase approach: (1) write-additive migration (write new format, keep read fallback), (2) read-switch with verification, (3) cleanup code-paths in later minor version.
- Always capture a snapshot before any DDL; test restore in staging.

KV cache and model cache considerations
- KV cache format must include proto-version field for safe decode. If upgrading cache format, run a cache-migration job that scans and upgrades keys with idempotency.
- If offline migration too slow, set cache TTLs low, spin the new runtime with cache-warmers for critical prefixes.

Control plane API compatibility checklist
- Contract: ensure API backwards-compatible (old clients should not get HTTP 4xx for existing routes).
- Feature gates: new endpoints behind feature flags.
- Agent handshake: version-negotiation header must be present; control plane must reject agents older than the minimum supported version with a clear error and repair docs link.

Observability and verification
- Enable synthetic traces targeting the canary cluster and compare traces with baseline by percent difference (trace similarity > 95%).
- Aggregated metrics to query immediately after canary start: requests_total, requests_5xx_total, token_latency_seconds{quantile=0.95}, kv_cache_miss_rate. Keep a recorded baseline from the last successful upgrade.
- Collect flamegraphs of top-5 inference hot paths in both versions for 10 minutes each.

Emergency rollback procedure (manual, if automated rollback fails)
1) Contact incident lead and authorizer.
2) Run: curl -X POST $ROUTER_API/set_weights -d '{"version":"baseline","weight":100}'.
3) Scale new instance group down via terraform or cloud API: terraform apply -var='scale_canary=0' --target=module.runtime_canary
4) Re-attach persistent volumes to baseline instances if any were moved.
5) Restore control-plane DB snapshot if corruption suspected (follow DB restore runbook).
6) Post-rollback, collect full diagnostics and open a postmortem ticket.

Post-upgrade validation and cleanup (24h)
- Keep old version artifacts (images, templates) in registry for 72h.
- Run a deeper regression suite against production traffic samples overnight (long-tail prompts).
- If everything stable for 24h, schedule decommissioning of standby baseline instances and remove temporary Terraform resources in a controlled apply.

Runbook snippets and useful commands
- Capture canary logs: kubectl -n runtime logs deployment/runtime-canary --since=1h | gzip > canary-logs-$(date -I).gz\- Set router weights (example):
curl -X POST https://router.private.redwood/api/v1/weights 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTER_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"service":"runtime","weights":{"v2":10,"v1":90}}'

- Terraform plan for nondestructive creation: terraform apply -var='upgrade_mode=gated-canary' -auto-approve

Open questions and cautions
- Need better automation for KV format migrations — currently still ad hoc on some customers.
- Metric baselines vary wildly by customer workload; a per-customer baseline capture in the preflight is mandatory.
- Network egress policies: some on-prem firewalls block image pulls; pre-verify registry access in the maintenance window.

Appendix: quick decision tree (text)
1) Are there stateful schema changes? -> Yes: schedule two-phase migration and extend maintenance window. No: follow gated canary.
2) Is the upgrade backwards compatible for agents? -> No: require agent-side rollout before control-plane upgrade.
3) Does terraform plan require resource replacement? -> Yes: prefer create-before-destroy pattern and explicit data replication.

Owners and roles
- Upgrade owner: Sasha Patel (executes and coordinates)
- Rollback owner: Diego Morales (authorizes and runs rollback)
- Observability lead: Asha Rao (validates metrics and gates)
- Terraform reviewer: Ben Thompson

Notes and next steps
- Convert these manual gates into a lightweight CI job that can run the preflight checks and produce a pass/fail report for the upgrade owner.
- Build a small migration utility for KV proto upgrades with dry-run and fix flags.
- Add an automated “canary weight controller” to minimize human latency when promoting/demoting traffic.

End of document
